sentences.text:
THIS CRIMINAL PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Heard Sri. S. Balakrishnan, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Vinayaka V.S., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the records.

2. Present petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. with the following prayer:
"WHEREFORE, the petitioner humbly prays that this Hon'ble court may be pleased to enlarge the petitioner on bail in Cr.No.162/2022 for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 304(B) of IPC and under Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, on the file of Sathanoor Police Station now numbered as S.C.No.5022/2022 pending before the II Addl. District and Sessions Judge at Kanakapura in the interest of justice and equity."

entities.text: II Addl. District and Sessions Judge at Kanakapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The brief facts of the case are as under:
Sri. Gurumurthy P, S/o Late Puttaswamy lodged a complaint with Sathanoor Police Station, Ramanagara District on 31.05.2023, which was registered in Crime No.162/2022 for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 304B of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC', for short) at the first instance.
4.

The gist of the complaint averments reveal that the elder sister of the complainant by name Smt.Mangalagowramma was married to the petitioner at about 2 years back and they were no issues in the wedlock.
Thereafter, the couple lived in the house of the complainant for about two years.
On 27.05.2022 at about 6.30 a.m., the petitioner and Smt.Mangalagowramma went to 'Mekedatu' a tourist place.
After spending sometime in the said place, while returning, on account of some frustration, Smt. Mangalagowramma fell into the river.
Thereafter, the petitioner proceeded to Sathanoor Police Station and intimated the incident.
Complainant was secured and he gave a complaint and the complaint came to be registered at the first instance as a missing complaint.
On 30.05.2022, Sathanoor Police asked the complainant through telephone to rush to the Police Station as they have spotted a floating dead body in the river.

The dead body that was spotted by the police had only half portion of the body i.e., below the trunk region and the complainant identified the Sri. Lakkappa @ Ramu vs The State Of Karnataka on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161488428/
2 same as that of his sister.

sentences.text: He expressed suspicion with regard to her death and also informed the police that there was harassment with regard to demand of dowry and sought for action.
5. Based on the said complaint, the police have registered a criminal case as aforesaid and investigated the matter.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner was apprehended and he was sent to judicial custody.
After investigation, the police have filed chargesheet against the accused for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 304B and 302 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

6. The attempt made by the petitioner to obtain an order of grant of regular bail in Crl.Misc.No.5355/2022 is turned down by the learned II Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Ramanagara, Sit at Kanakapura by order dated 08.11.2022 and thereafter, the present petitioner is before this Court.

entities.text:
Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Ramanagara, Sit at Kanakapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. Sri.S.Balakrishnan, learned Counsel for the petitioner reiterating the grounds urged in the bail petition, vehemently contended that it is the petitioner who made a search for the body of his wife and when he was not able to trace the same, he went to Sathanoor Police and intimated the police about missing of his wife and thereafter the police have secured the presence of the complainant on 27.05.2022 and have registered a missing complaint.

8. He further contended that as an afterthought when a portion of the dead body was found, the complainant in order to take advantage of the same, lodged a false complainant stating that there was a demand of dowry and then, police registered the case for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 304B of IPC, which is per se incorrect inasmuch as there is no previous complaint or panchayath with regard to the demand of dowry and therefore, the case of the prosecution is per se concocted and sought for grant of bail.
9.

He also contended that the fact of lodging belated complaint is an afterthought and after due deliberation with the relatives, friends and advisors and if there was a demand of dowry, nothing prevented the complainant to express the same before the police on 27.05.2022 itself and therefore,
sought for grant of bail.
10.
Per contra, learned HCGP reiterating the grounds urged in the objection statement opposed the bail grounds.

11. He contended that if the petitioner is so innocent as he is contending, nothing prevented him to lodge the complaint himself and there was no necessity of securing the presence of the complainant on 27.05.2022.

He further contended that since the offence punishable under Sections 304B and 302 of IPC are invoked, the gravity of the offence is on the higher side and the unnatural death of the wife of the petitioner having taken place within seven years of the marriage, the presumption is available to the prosecution under Sections 113A and 113B of the Indian Evidence Act.
12. Therefore, prima-facie the contention of the petitioner that he is innocent of the offences alleged against him is pressed into service and sought for rejection of the bail.

sentences.text: In the light of the rival contentions, this Court perused the materials on record meticulously.
14. On such perusal of the materials on record, it is seen that in the marriage there were no issues.
What prompted the petitioner to take the wife to Mekedatu on 27.05.2022 is not forthcoming on record.

Any way, the fact remains that soon after the wife of the petitioner slipped into the river as is contended by the petitioner, immediately, the petitioner went to Sathanoor Police Station and informed about the incident.
But, he failed to inform the complainant, more so, when the petitioner had taken shelter in the house of the complainant itself.

15. Instead of informing the complainant, who is none other than the younger brother of the wife of the petitioner, the petitioner took his own sweet time and went to the police station and informed about missing of his wife.

It is pertinent to note that the distance within the place of incident and Sathanoor Police Station is more than 25 kms. and it would take at least one hour to reach the place having regard to the available transport at the spot.
According to the petitioner, it is thereafter, the complainant was secured to the Police Station as missing complaint came to be lodged.

16. The petitioner urged that if there was a demand of dowry, the complainant would have definitely revealed the same to the police on 27.05.2022 itself and having taken time till 30.05.2022 and lodging the complaint of demand of dowry raises suspicion about the bonafides of the complaint averments.

17. It is settled principles of law and requires no emphasis that the court at the stage of considering bail request, cannot hold a mini trial to find out the merits of the case as the same may be prejudice to the case of the parties in one way or other.

18. Suffice to say that the conduct of the petitioner in not informing the incident to the complainant at the first instance and going to the police station and informing about missing of his wife, raises sufficient suspicion about the bonafides of the petitioner as well.
19.
Any way, it is for the trial Court to form a definite opinion as to the case of the prosecution after full-fledged trial.

Suffice to say that since the death has taken place within seven years of the marriage, as rightly contended on behalf of the prosecution, the prosecution enjoys the presumption of Sections 113A and 113B of the Indian Evidence Act.
Further, what is traced by the police is the portion of the dead body.

If somebody has slipped into the river and the dead body is found at a later point of time, how only the portion of the body would be available is a question that would also be enquired into and decided by the trial court.

21. Taking note of these aspects of the matter, this Court is of the considered opinion that it is too premature for this Court to express any opinion about that case of the prosecution or the defence as portrayed on behalf of the petitioner.

4 22.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At least till the examination of the material witnesses, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner cannot be enlarged on bail by resorting to the special powers vested in this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., moreso, when after tracing a portion of the dead body, police have also invoked the offence under Section 302 of IPC., by filing the charge sheet.

Reserving such liberty for the petitioner to file a fresh bail petition, if there is a positive changed circumstances in this case, the following order is passed;
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is Rejected.
